newsitem.title: JAPAN: Crudes falls in Asia as May contract expires.
newsitem.headline: Crudes falls in Asia as May contract expires.

text.p: Crude oil prices eased in the late Asian market on Tuesday with the market quiet ahead of the expiry of the prompt May contract, traders said.
June cash Brent was notionally assessed at $18.30/18.35 per barrel in late Tokyo trading.
In paper spreads a European major sold the May/June Brent spread at minus 30 cents to a trader, compared to late U.S. trading levels of minus 25 cents to minus 26 cents.
The June Brent/Dubai spread was notionally assessed at $1.38/1.43, while the July spread was notionally assessed at $1.50/1.60.
Activity in the physical market was quiet, with June Oman bid at a discount of 10 cents to the official selling price and offered at a discount of four cents to MPM, traders said.

They said, however, that the indications did not appear to be very firm. Most traders discounted a vague rumour that a June Oman had been sold by a Japanese trader at MPM minus two cents, partly because the price did not reflect the current June market for the medium crude.
Some traders said there was a report that a 450,000-barrel June Masila had been exchanged at a premium of 12 to 13 cents to the official selling price.
Traders were mixed in their outlook for June Abu Dhabi crude grades.

Some traders said though the crude still looked slightly weak, they expected to see a slight improvement in premiums for June cargoes. They expect firmer buying demand with the return of many refineries in the region from scheduled maintenances. Other traders said requirments for the month appeared light.

In Asian crudes, Minas appeared to be supported by expectations that buying interest would emerge from China, South Korea and possibly by Japanese traders. The crude was assessed as fetching ICP plus 5 to 10 cents.--M.Yoshikawa/Tokyo
